title: Nashville hot chicken
subtitle: Chilli-oil-soaked fried chicken on white bread with pickles
excerpt: Nashville hot chicken is fried chicken pieces dipped immediately after frying into a paste of lard, cayenne, and brown sugar. The coating soaks into the crust as it cools. Served on slices of plain white bread with dill pickle slices, the bread absorbs the dripping spiced oil. Heat level is customisable.
sourceNotes: Nashville, Tennessee culinary tradition. Nashville hot chicken is attributed to Thornton Prince of Prince's Hot Chicken Shack (established 1930s), where the dish has been made in largely the same way ever since. Background from WPA Tennessee food surveys and contemporary documentation of the Prince's recipe.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chicken must soak in buttermilk for at least 4 hours.

content.text: Nashville hot chicken uses the same buttermilk-brined double-dredge method as Southern fried chicken, then immediately after frying brushes the pieces with a paste of cayenne, brown sugar, garlic powder, and hot frying oil. The paste soaks into the crust and turns it deep orange-red. Served on plain white bread with sliced pickles, the bread catches the dripping oil.

items.prepNote: plain white sliced bread, to serve

content.text: Soak the chicken pieces in {{buttermilk}} of buttermilk with a tablespoon of salt for at least 4 hours in the fridge. Mix {{plain-flour}} of flour with {{garlic-powder}} of garlic powder, {{paprika-smoked}} of smoked paprika, the remaining salt, and {{black-pepper}} of black pepper. Double-dredge as for the fried chicken recipe: flour, back into buttermilk, flour again.
Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil to 170°C in the Dutch oven. Fry in batches for 12 to 14 minutes until deep golden and the internal temperature reads 75°C. Drain on a rack.

While the last batch fries, mix together {{cayenne-pepper}} of cayenne, {{light-brown-sugar}} of brown sugar, the extra {{garlic-powder}} of garlic powder, the extra {{paprika-smoked}} of smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt in a small heatproof bowl. Ladle 4 tablespoons of the hot frying oil over the paste and stir to combine. Brush generously over each piece of chicken immediately.
Serve each piece on a slice of white bread with sliced pickles on top. The bread is the plate.

items.symptom: Paste too liquid and runs off
items.cause: Too much hot oil added to the paste.
items.fix: Start with 3 tablespoons of hot oil and add the fourth only if the paste is still too thick to brush.

items.cause: 3 teaspoons of cayenne is genuine Nashville medium heat.
items.fix: Reduce cayenne to 1 teaspoon for mild, or substitute paprika for some of the cayenne.

content.text: Boneless thigh fillets cooked in a similar way make a sandwich version. The hot paste can be mixed with melted butter instead of frying oil for a slightly milder, richer result. A drizzle of honey over the dressed chicken softens the heat and adds gloss.

Nashville hot chicken is a dish of such specific character that it has almost no parallel in world cooking. The combination of deeply fried, crisp chicken soaked in a hot, sweet paste and set on plain white bread is exactly what it needs to be and nothing more. Prince's Hot Chicken Shack has been making it in Nashville since the 1930s with barely any change to the original recipe.
